title: All Verus specs are commented-out (non-functional)
detail: All verus! blocks in durability_matrix.verus, types_eventseq.verus, and append_strict_journaled.verus are fully commented with //. Verus will not parse commented code. 6/27 obligations produce zero verification. Critical INV-002, POST-001/002/006/007 are unverified.
fix: Uncomment all verus! blocks. Add verus! macro to source files at artifact paths. Verify Verus parses each module.
contract_parity: no — verus lane produces no evidence

title: AppendStrict IF TRUE makes barrier always succeed — failure path unreachable
detail: JournalBarrier.tla AppendStrict action has IF TRUE, making the persist success branch always taken and the failure path (ELSE with persistError=TRUE) unreachable. The contract requires that append_strict returns Ok(()) only after BOTH append_unpersisted AND persist_strict succeed. The model never exercises the case where append succeeds but barrier fails, so I1/I2 are not fully verified for that path.
fix: Replace IF TRUE with a model variable persistSucceeds:BOOLEAN and drive both branches via state transitions

title: CompleteFlush reachable without appending events — QF1 vacuous
detail: QueuedStrictFlush.tla CompleteFlush action has no pre-condition requiring all queued strict events to be appended. It clears queue'={} and sets strictFlushComplete'=TRUE. QF1 checks strictFlushComplete in the resulting state where queue'=empty, making the universal quantifier vacuously true. A non-conforming implementation that returns success without appending passes QF1.
fix: Add pre-condition to CompleteFlush requiring all strict events appended, or split into AppendAllStrict+CompleteFlush with QF1 checking pre-condition
contract_parity: no — QF1/QF2 do not verify DISPATCH-002 flush ordering
bounds: CompleteFlush reachable with appendedEvents subset of queued events

title: Dispatch harnesses are vacuous — kani::any() then trivially re-check same match
detail: Both dispatch harnesses use kani::any() to pick a profile, matches! to test it, then kani::assert(re-checks same match). The actual dispatch logic (if profile==Strict then append_strict else append_journaled) is never called or verified. These are not valid verification artifacts.
fix: Rewrite harnesses to construct StorageRuntimeJournal with each profile and actually call append_storage_event to verify dispatch behavior

title: Placeholder harness asserting true — RECOVERY-002 not verified
detail: verify_hydrate_run_frame_digest_matches.rs line 36: kani::assert(true, ...). This produces zero verification evidence. The harness does not create a journal, call recover_runtime_frame_seed_from_events, or assert any digest match. Indistinguishable from a trivially-correct proof.
fix: Write real Kani harness: create journal with known events, call recover_runtime_frame_seed_from_events, assert digest matches expected header digest

title: Placeholder harness asserting true — RECOVERY-003 not verified
detail: verify_replay_divergence_detected.rs line 28: kani::assert(true, ...). Produces zero verification evidence. Does not construct out-of-order events or call replay_events to verify ReplayDivergence detection.
fix: Write real Kani harness: construct out-of-order event sequence, call replay_events, assert Err(ReplayDivergence)

title: Integration tests are non-executing stubs — only construct error variants
detail: All four integration tests only construct RuntimeError variants (let _err = RuntimeError::...). They do not call the runtime, inject failures, or verify ack behavior. These will compile but never fail and never verify FAIL-001 or ACK-ORDER-001. OQ-3 (test_evidence paths) cannot be answered.
fix: Write real behavioral tests with mock FjallJournal fixtures that inject persist failures and verify typed error propagation with no ack sent
bounds: stub tests always pass without exercising runtime

title: Loom tests use #[test] not #[loom::test] — not actual concurrency models
detail: All four tests in queue_concurrency.rs use #[test] and thread::spawn (real threads). Loom requires #[loom::test] annotation and loom::thread::spawn to explore thread interleavings. With #[test], cargo loom will not explore permutations and the concurrency model is not exercised. The proof-writer report incorrectly claims these are loom tests.
fix: Re-annotate all tests with #[loom::test] and replace thread::spawn with loom::thread::spawn

title: event_seq_monotonic uses ==> which can be vacuous
detail: proptestCases/event_seq_ordering.rs uses prop_assert!(v1 < v2 ==> { ... }). When v1 >= v2, the ==> short-circuits to Ok(()). Proptest generates cases where antecedent holds, but this is non-idiomatic. The property is not maximally discriminating.
fix: Use proptest::prop_assume!(v1 < v2) before the assertion to filter pairs, then assert monotonicity unconditionally
bounds: v1 >= v2 cases produce no test signal

title: proof_matrix_completeness calls undefined assert_seqs_equal()
detail: durability_matrix.verus line 65: assert_seqs_equal() is called in a by{} block but this function does not exist in Verus standard library. If the verus! block were uncommented, this would cause a Verus compilation error.
fix: Remove assert_seqs_equal() call; use direct structural assertions for set equality

title: INV-004 serde roundtrip modeled as identity not tested in TLA
detail: EventSeqOrdering.tla models serde roundtrip as identity (EO3=TRUE with comment). This is an acceptable simplification but does not exercise a real serialize→deserialize sequence. INV-004 coverage depends on Miri and Proptest lanes.
fix: Covered by MIRI-CODEC-001 and PROPTEST-EVENTSEQ-001 if those lanes work. Acceptable as TLA simplification if documented.
contract_parity: partial — identity model vs actual serde
bounds: serde not exercised in TLA model

title: Hardcoded RecordKind variant list may diverge from actual enum
detail: verify_record_kind_codec.rs hardcodes 21 RecordKind variants. If the actual RecordKind enum in vb_storage/src/records.rs has different variants or discriminants, harness will fail to compile or miss coverage. Should auto-discover variants via derive, not hand-maintain a list.
fix: Derive VariantNames or use const generic to auto-enumerate RecordKind variants
contract_parity: partial — depends on manual list staying in sync
